correct_completion: has a single policy decision been scrutinised so thoroughly.
full_sentence: Rarely, if ever, has a single policy decision been scrutinised so thoroughly.
acceptable_variants: has any policy decision been examined so closely.
has a government decision faced such intense scrutiny.

options.text: a policy decision has been so thoroughly scrutinised.
options.why_wrong: Without inversion after the fronted negative adverbial, the sentence is a neutral statement and loses the emphatic effect that 'rarely, if ever' sets up.

options.text: has a single policy decision been scrutinised so thoroughly.
the public has rarely scrutinised policy decisions.
options.why_wrong: This repeats 'rarely' in neutral word order and turns the stem into a general habit, not a fronted emphatic clause about one decision.

options.text: so a single policy decision was scrutinised thoroughly.
options.why_wrong: 'So' introduces a result clause, but the stem sets up a fronted negative adverbial, which requires an inverted question-like clause rather than a consequence.

grammar_focus: Subject-auxiliary inversion after fronted negative adverbials ('Rarely, if ever, has...')
explanation: Fronting a negative adverbial such as 'rarely' triggers subject-auxiliary inversion, so the auxiliary 'has' must come before the subject. Learners often keep neutral word order here because their first language marks emphasis mainly through word order and intonation rather than obligatory auxiliary inversion.
translation: Rzadko, o ile w ogóle, jakakolwiek pojedyncza decyzja polityczna była analizowana tak dokładnie.
